ideas.description: On the tip (E034 commit f74c715: Muon NS3 batched and compiled, lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, whitening bias trained only in epoch 1, 6.5 epochs; or I041's successor if it is kept), make one change: lower the BatchNorm-bias lr multiplier in the SGD group from x64 to x32. Keep lr*wd constant for the BN biases by doubling their wd, so the per-step decay is unchanged. The head lr, whitening-bias lr, Muon, lookahead, LS, augmentation and epochs all stay identical. This does not depend on I044 (head lr x0.5); the two test different parts of the SGD group and can run in either order. Rationale: x64 was tuned for CIFAR-10 SGD airbench, where the conv filters moved at SGD rates. Under Muon with weight-norm projection, the filters rotate at a fixed relative rate, so BN biases at x64 may now dominate how fast the features shift. Pass the lr as a 0-d tensor so nothing recompiles; no new shapes are needed.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.35 to +0.4 pp, point +0.05 pp (range 0.751-0.759 around tip 0.7551). Time unchanged within ±1.5% (~5.89 s). A gain of 0.25 pp or more supports H1.7.1 and banks ~0.25 epoch (~3.5% time); retry 6.25 epochs next. A drop of 0.25 pp or more means the biases want a larger lr; the follow-up is x128 (one run). If the result is within ±0.25 pp and I044 is also neutral, the SGD group is flat and H1.7.1 is refuted.

ideas.description: Explore selective backprop without a proxy model (H1.4.1 has no test yet). On the tip, after the first epoch (the existing switch point where the whitening bias freezes), change each training step as follows. (1) Run a no-grad forward of the full 1024-image augmented batch through the compiled eval-mode graph, which uses the BN running stats and changes no state. (2) Compute the per-sample label-smoothed CE and take the top 512 indices with torch.topk. (3) Gather those 512 images and labels and run the normal compiled train step (forward, backward, Muon, SGD, lookahead) on them; the loss is the mean over the 512. The final partial batch of 848 selects 424. Epoch 1 stays at full batch, as now. The number of steps, the per-step lr schedules (Muon lr 0.16, SGD-group per-step lr) and the lookahead sync every 5 steps are unchanged, as are the epochs (6.5) and the sample stream. Compile and warm up in build() on synthetic data, using channels_last tensors of the exact layout used in the timed path (E035 lesson): the 512 and 424 train-step shapes (without whitening-bias grad), the eval-mode scoring forward at 1024 and 848, and topk/gather. Run drafts/debug_nan.py on the new train shapes under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, and compare trial-0 and later-trial train times in the result to catch warmup gaps.
ideas.expected: Time -10% to -17%, point -13% (~5.13 s). The scoring forward costs ~1/3 of a step and the 512-sample step ~1/2, on ~85% of steps; the Muon/lookahead overhead is unchanged. Accuracy -1.6 to -0.3 pp, point -0.9 pp: the regime is step-limited, so steps are kept, but each gradient sees half the samples and BN batch stats come from a hard-skewed subset. That is probably infeasible on its own. At the knee an epoch is worth ~1.14 pp for ~15% time, so break-even is about -1.0 pp. A drop of 0.7 pp or less supports H1.4.1; then add epochs at the cheaper per-step cost (e.g. 7.0 epochs, ~5.5 s) to bank a net ~5-7% gain. A drop of 1.2 pp or more refutes H1.4.1 at this horizon and closes example selection.

ideas.description: Probe the batch-size axis in the direction opposite I042, so that both together pin the accuracy-vs-batch slope at a fixed epoch count. D009 C0110 says the optimal batch grows with horizon, so at ~320 steps it may be below 1024. On the tip, change only the batch size from 1024 to 768 at 6.5 epochs (~424 steps instead of ~319), with every schedule (lr warmup/decay, Muon lr, lookahead (t/T)^3 ramp) scaled to the new step count. The Muon lr stays 0.16 and momentum 0.8 (normalized updates). For the SGD group (BN biases, whitening bias, head): if the code uses airbench's per-example lr normalization, keep the configured values; otherwise scale the per-step lr x0.75 and keep lr*wd constant. Lookahead still syncs every 5 steps. The whitening bias trains for the first epoch, measured in samples (~65 steps). Compile and warm up the 768 full batch and the new final partial batch (50000 mod 768 = 80) for both train-step variants in build(), using channels_last tensors of the exact timed layout. Run debug_nan.py on the new shapes. This runs regardless of I042's outcome; its information value is independent.
ideas.expected: Time +3% to +8%, point +5% (~6.19 s): ~105 more steps of Muon/SGD/lookahead overhead (~2 ms each, ~0.2 s) plus slightly worse GEMM efficiency. Accuracy -0.2 to +0.7 pp, point +0.25 pp, since 33% more fixed-magnitude Muon rotations help a step-starved run. At the epoch rate (~0.076 pp per 1% time), the change is a net win only if the gain is 0.45 pp or more. If so, keep it and cut to ~6.0 epochs (net ~-3%), which supports a small critical batch and refutes H1.2.3's direction. A gain under 0.2 pp means per-sample efficiency is flat between 768 and 1024, which raises I042's prior. A drop of 0.2 pp or more means 1024 is at or below the optimum.

- I043 (brightness/contrast jitter).
